extracted.intended_audience: interested parties to the FCC rulemaking (broadcasters, licensees, counsel, and members of the public who may file comments)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements associated with filing comments and participating in an FCC notice-and-comment rulemaking (here: proposed amendment to 47 CFR part 73 for Cape Girardeau television allotments). Includes deadlines, filing addresses, ex parte restrictions, technical rule citations, and accessibility/administrative notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments filing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be filed on or before August 8, 2024 and reply comments on or before August 23, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the DATES section for filing deadlines. The document also states 'Comments are no longer being accepted. See DATES for details.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to file comments (filing addresses / service)
rubrics_metrics.description: File comments with the Federal Communications Commission, Office of the Secretary, 45 L Street NE, Washington, DC 20554. In addition to filing comments with the FCC, interested parties should serve counsel for the Petitioner as follows: Joan Stewart, Esq., Wiley Rein, LLP, 1776 K Street NW, Washington, DC 20006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the addresses provided for both filing and serving opposing parties/counsel. See §§1.415 and 1.420 of the Commission's rules for information regarding proper filing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Commission filing procedures (§§1.415 and 1.420)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must use the proper filing procedures for comments as set forth in 47 CFR 1.415 and 1.420.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice refers readers to §§1.415 and 1.420 for details on proper filing procedures (formats, electronic submission, service requirements, and related procedural rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte contacts prohibition (47 CFR 1.1208)
rubrics_metrics.description: All ex parte contacts are prohibited from the time a notice of proposed rulemaking is issued to the time the matter is no longer subject to Commission consideration or court review, see 47 CFR 1.1208.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are exceptions to this prohibition, which can be found in §1.1204(a) of the Commission's rules. Parties should consult §1.1204(a) to determine whether any communication falls within an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act plain-language summary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act requires each agency, in providing notice of a rulemaking, to post online a brief plain-language summary of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required summary of this notice is available at https://www.fcc.gov/proposed-rulemakings. Agencies must make a plain-language summary publicly accessible in accordance with the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To request materials in accessible formats (braille, large print, computer diskettes, or audio recordings), contact FCC504@fcc.gov or call the Consumer & Government Affairs Bureau at (202) 418-0530 (VOICE), (202) 418-0432 (TTY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the requested accessible format type when contacting the FCC. This is the channel to obtain alternative-format versions of rulemaking materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act / Small Business Paperwork Relief Act / Regulatory Flexibility Act applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This document does not contain information collection requirements subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, and therefore does not contain any proposed information collection burden 'for small business concerns with fewer than 25 employees,' pursuant to the Small Business Paperwork Relief Act of 2002; Provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980 do not apply to this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explicitly states that PRA and RFA requirements are not triggered for this action; parties should not expect new information-collection burdens or RFA analyses in this document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official legal format / verification against official Federal Register edition
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays an XML rendition that is not an official legal edition. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar (on govinfo.gov) for the official electronic format. Only official editions of the Federal Register provide legal notice to the public and judicial notice to the courts under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on the document for legal research or formal purposes, verify contents against the official print/PDF edition on govinfo.gov (FR Doc. 2024-15040). The XML/prototype site is informational only until ACFR grants official status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical compliance criteria for channel substitution (§73.618(a) and §73.622(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission finds the proposed channel substitution warrants consideration and that, given Gray proposes to utilize its currently licensed parameters, channel 11 can be substituted for channel 32 at Cape Girardeau in compliance with the principal community coverage requirements of §73.618(a) and the technical requirements set forth in §73.622(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice specifies coordinates (37-25′-44.7″ N and 089-30′-14.2″ W) and that the proposal uses currently licensed technical parameters; applicants and commenters should assess compliance with §73.618(a) (principal community coverage) and §73.622(a) technical rules when evaluating or proposing substitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document heading/content conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings may contain: the agency or agencies that issued and signed a document; the number of the CFR title and the number of each part the document amends, proposes to amend, or is directly related to; the agency docket number / agency internal file number; the RIN which identifies each regulatory action listed in the Unified Agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This repetition of headings forms internal navigation links and has no substantive legal effect. See the Document Drafting Handbook for more details on drafting headings and document structure.
